record.context_brief: Alternative proof strategy for cubic-threefold Torelli
record.original_question: Can the categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds, namely Theorem 5.4, be proved by using the extension techniques for Fourier-Mukai equivalences that are discussed in Section 3.1?

evidence.quote: Question 5.6. Is it possible to prove Theorem 5.4 by using the extension techniques that we discussed in Section 3.1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{P}^4_{\mathbb{C}}$ be a smooth cubic threefold. The bounded derived category $\mathrm{D}^b(Y)$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$\mathrm{D}^b(Y) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(Y), \mathcal{O}_Y, \mathcal{O}_Y(1) \rangle,$$
where the Kuznetsov component $\mathcal{K}u(Y)$ is defined as the right orthogonal of $\langle \mathcal{O}_Y, \mathcal{O}_Y(1)\rangle$. The categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds asserts that for two smooth complex cubic threefolds $Y$ and $Y'$, an equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(Y) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(Y')$ of $\mathbb{C}$-linear triangulated categories (of Fourier–Mukai type) implies that $Y \cong Y'$ as projective varieties.

A general "extension technique" for Fourier–Mukai equivalences provides criteria under which an exact equivalence $\Phi : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{A}'$ between admissible subcategories $\mathcal{A} \subset \mathrm{D}^b(X)$ and $\mathcal{A}' \subset \mathrm{D}^b(X')$ appearing in semiorthogonal decompositions can be lifted to an equivalence $\widetilde{\Phi} : \mathrm{D}^b(X) \to \mathrm{D}^b(X')$ of the ambient derived categories.

Problem. Using only such extension techniques for Fourier–Mukai equivalences (i.e. extending a given equivalence $\mathcal{K}u(Y) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(Y')$ to an equivalence $\mathrm{D}^b(Y) \simeq \mathrm{D}^b(Y')$ and then invoking Bondal–Orlov reconstruction), give a proof of the categorical Torelli theorem for smooth complex cubic threefolds.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2023/2024 paper by Z. Liu, "On Fourier–Mukai type autoequivalences of Kuznetsov components of cubic threefolds" (Math. Nachr., 2024), provides an alternative proof of the Fourier–Mukai version of the categorical Torelli theorem for smooth complex cubic threefolds by extending Fourier–Mukai equivalences between Kuznetsov components to equivalences of the ambient derived categories, exactly along the lines requested. Subsequent work (e.g. on non-Eckardt cubic threefolds via equivariant Kuznetsov components) further develops this strategy.

status_evidence.title: On Fourier-Mukai type autoequivalences of Kuznetsov components of cubic threefolds
status_evidence.snippet: We determine the group of all Fourier-Mukai type autoequivalences of Kuznetsov components of smooth complex cubic threefolds, and provide yet another proof for the Fourier-Mukai version of categorical Torelli theorem for smooth complex cubic threefolds.
status_evidence.claim: Liu gives an alternative proof of the Fourier–Mukai categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds via extension of equivalences.

status_evidence.title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: A general criterion allows extending Fourier–Mukai equivalences among admissible subcategories appearing in semiorthogonal decompositions; cubic threefolds satisfy categorical Torelli with no further assumptions on the equivalence.
status_evidence.claim: Extension techniques for Fourier–Mukai equivalences yield categorical Torelli for cubic threefolds.

status_evidence.title: Three approaches to a categorical Torelli theorem for cubic threefolds of non-Eckardt type via the equivariant Kuznetsov components
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a third proof using equivariant Kuznetsov components and extension of Fourier–Mukai equivalences.
status_evidence.claim: Further work confirms the extension-based strategy works for cubic threefolds.
